notes: Test cases for the skill-creator eval loop. Run each with a Fable-powered agent WITH the skill vs. a Fable baseline WITHOUT it. Each needs a target repo — ideally one with a distinctive domain (multi-tenant, healthcare, payments, AI) so we can judge whether the derived review areas are custom to that codebase, plus a few known/planted issues to measure catch-rate. Assertions are drafts; refine after the user signs off on prompts and picks target repos.

evals.prompt: Do a thorough audit of this codebase — security, correctness, architecture, and code quality. I want a report I can hand to my team.
evals.expected_output: A docs/review/fable/ directory: an index fable-review.md plus one fable-review-NN-<slug>.md per review area, where the areas are derived from THIS codebase's domain and architecture (not a generic checklist). Index has exec summary + findings-at-a-glance table + area map + top risks + system-level assessment + coverage/method. Fan-out (one agent per area) + a separate verification pass actually happened.
assertions: Creates a docs/review/fable/ directory at the repo root with an index fable-review.md
Produces multiple fable-review-NN-<slug>.md area files, zero-padded and numbered in priority order
At least one area file is specific to this codebase's domain/architecture, not a generic dimension (e.g. tenant-isolation, hipaa, ai-layer, money-handling — whatever fits this repo)
The index contains: executive summary, findings-at-a-glance table, area map linking to each area file, top risks, system-level assessment, coverage/method
Each area file has scope, an area-health summary, and severity-ranked findings tagged with a dimension
The index glance-table totals reconcile with the sum of the per-area finding counts
Every reported finding cites a concrete file:line location
Findings use only the rubric severity labels (Critical/High/Medium/Low/Info)
No source files under audit were modified (git diff shows only docs/review/fable/ added)
The run spawned parallel per-area review subagents and a separate verification pass

Areas are reviewed THROUGH the four-dimension lens (security, correctness, architecture, maintainability) — findings carry dimension tags and the rubric was applied; a legitimately single-dimension area (e.g. a dependencies/supply-chain sweep) need not surface a finding in all four

evals.prompt: We're acquiring this company and I need a due-diligence review of their backend before we sign. Focus me on the real risks — I don't want an 80-item nitpick list, I want to know what would actually hurt us.
evals.expected_output: A docs/review/fable/ collection whose index leads hard with impact: a short prioritized top-risks section and a system-level tech-debt/architecture read, area files ordered with the highest-stakes areas first (fable-review-01-*), serious findings verified, low-value nitpicks suppressed or grouped, blind spots stated honestly in the coverage section.
assertions: Index top-risks section is present and prioritized by impact, not volume, and links into the relevant area files
Area files are numbered so the highest-stakes areas come first
Critical/High findings are marked as verified
The collection does not bury serious findings under a long list of Low/Info items
Index coverage/method section honestly states what was and wasn't reviewed
System-level assessment discusses tech-debt hotspots (churn x complexity)

evals.prompt: Just started at this job and inherited this repo. Can you review the whole thing and tell me where the bodies are buried, what's fragile, and what I should be scared to touch?
evals.expected_output: An onboarding-oriented docs/review/fable/ collection: the area map plus system-level assessment give a new engineer a mental model of how the codebase decomposes, area files emphasize fragile / high-churn hotspots while still surfacing security and correctness landmines, everything file-linked and honestly scoped.
assertions: The area map in the index gives a new engineer a clear decomposition of the codebase
Report identifies fragile / high-churn / high-complexity hotspots explicitly (in the relevant area files and/or system assessment)
System-level assessment explains how the codebase is structured and where seams have eroded
Security and correctness findings still surfaced across the area files, not dropped in favor of only architecture
Findings link to file:line so a new engineer can navigate to them
